content:
With WhatsApp officially rolling out its username feature, users can now store a username in addition to a name and phone number when saving a contact. Here are the details.

The new username field feature is gradually being rolled out to some WhatsApp users.

Although usernames are a basic feature on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun moving away from relying entirely on phone numbers to identify users.

WhatsApp had earlier begun rolling out a username reservation system, allowing users to register their preferred username in advance to prevent impersonation or scams when the feature officially launches.

A few weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has begun supporting users filling in a username field when adding new contacts. The field appears between the name field and the phone number field.

WABetaInfo reports:

WABetaInfo points out that the username field appears to be gradually rolling out to select users on both the WhatsApp beta and stable versions.

When I tested it on the latest stable version, although the field was displayed, the system still showed a message saying "This username is not on WhatsApp," even though the username actually exists.

Nonetheless, this feature marks WhatsApp finally catching up with its competitors by introducing a feature that many people felt should have been launched long ago.
